proposals.before: The prince withdrew, pressed tens of thousands of market dwellers into service, and marched to the western portal of Weiyang Palace. There he collided with the chancellor's host. For five days the armies slaughtered each other until corpses choked the canals and blood ran in the gutters.
proposals.after: The prince withdrew, pressed tens of thousands of market dwellers into service, and marched to the western portal of Changle Palace. There he collided with the chancellor's host. For five days the armies slaughtered each other until corpses choked the canals and blood ran in the gutters.
proposals.reason: Chinese 長樂西闕 is the west watchtower/gate of Changle Palace, not Weiyang Palace.

proposals.before: The heir led his troops away, drove the people of the four markets—several tens of thousands in all—to the west gate of Weiyang Palace, met the chancellor's army, and fought for five days; several tens of thousands died, and blood flowed into the ditches.
proposals.after: The heir led his troops away, drove the people of the four markets—several tens of thousands in all—to the west gate of Changle Palace, met the chancellor's army, and fought for five days; several tens of thousands died, and blood flowed into the ditches.
proposals.reason: The literal English likewise substitutes Weiyang for 長樂.

proposals.before: The following year General-in-chief Li Guangli marched against the Xiongnu. The chancellor saw him off with the road sacrifice as far as the Wei Bridge and there clasped hands in farewell.
proposals.after: The following year Ershi General Li Guangli marched against the Xiongnu. The chancellor saw him off with the road sacrifice as far as the Wei Bridge and there clasped hands in farewell.
proposals.reason: 貳師將軍 is the Ershi General, not Grand General (大將軍); General-in-chief conflates the titles.

proposals.before: for the Son of Heaven's son who kills someone by mistake, what sentence of dismissal applies!
proposals.after: for the Son of Heaven's son who kills someone by mistake, what punishment could possibly apply!
proposals.reason: 罷 here means what penalty could apply, not official dismissal.

proposals.before: The prince of Changyi, rushed to the capital, proved a debauchee on the throne. Huo Guang and chariot general Zhang Anshi resolved to pull him down and choose a worthier Liu.
proposals.after: The prince of Changyi, rushed to the capital, proved a debauchee on the throne. Huo Guang and chariot general Zhang Anshi resolved to pull him down and enthrone another.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 廢王更立 does not name the Liu clan; ‘a worthier Liu’ is an invented referent.

proposals.before: When Tian returned, husband and wife whispered their assent with him; Yang then obeyed Huo Guang's orders, and the coalition deposed the king of Changyi and raised Liu Bingyi as Xuandi.
proposals.after: When Tian returned, husband and wife whispered their assent with him; Yang then obeyed Huo Guang's orders, and the coalition deposed the king of Changyi and established Emperor Xuandi.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 立宣帝 does not give the personal name Liu Bingyi.

proposals.before: When the marquis of Gaochang's carriage bolted through the north vee gate, Yun remarked to Zhang Yanshou of Fuping, "They say the last time a team careered into a palace gate, the bar snapped, the horses fell, and Emperor Zhao was dead within days.
proposals.after: When the marquis of Gaochang's carriage bolted through the north side gate, Yun remarked to Zhang Yanshou of Fuping, "They say the last time a team careered into a palace gate, the bar snapped, the horses fell, and Emperor Zhao was dead within days.
proposals.reason: 北掖門 is a palace side gate; ‘vee’ is a corruption, not a translation of 掖.

proposals.before: Commandant Yu Dinggu questioned him until the corroborating testimony was plain, then reported to the throne:
proposals.after: Commandant Yu Dingguo questioned him until the corroborating testimony was plain, then reported to the throne:
proposals.reason: 廷尉定國 is Yu Dingguo; ‘Dinggu’ drops the final syllable.

proposals.before: The Commandant of Justice, Yu Dinggu, examined him; corroboration gathered on every side was clear, and he memorialized:
proposals.after: The Commandant of Justice, Yu Dingguo, examined him; corroboration gathered on every side was clear, and he memorialized:
proposals.reason: Same error as the idiomatic line: 定國 should be Dingguo.

proposals.before: Several slave-girl singers; after wine, ears hot, he faced heaven, beat the earthen jar, and cried 'wuwu day.'
proposals.after: Several slave-girl singers; after wine, ears hot, he faced heaven, beat the earthen jar, and cried 'wu-wu.'
proposals.reason: 呼烏烏 is an onomatopoeic Qin refrain, not the English word day.

proposals.before: The poem says: 'I farm that southern hill; weeds choke it untended; I sowed a hundred qing of beans—they fell and turned to beanstalks.
proposals.after: The poem says: 'I farm that southern hill; weeds choke it untended; I sowed one qing of beans—they fell and turned to beanstalks.
proposals.reason: Chinese 種一頃豆 is one qing, not a hundred.

proposals.before: Xian had always been on good terms with Yun; Yun had him watched and instructed to memorialize in self-defence.
proposals.after: Xian had always been on good terms with Yun; Yun, having inquired through informants, was instructed to memorialize in self-defence.
proposals.reason: 雲從刺候，教令上書自訟: Zhu Yun inquires and is told to self-defend; the literal reverses agency.

proposals.before: Che Qianqiu stood where yiyin day and Lü Wang once stood, yet at the hub of power he sealed his lips like a tied purse, never counseled aloud, saved his skin, and withdrew—such men!
proposals.after: Che Qianqiu stood where Yi Yin and Lü Wang once stood, yet at the hub of power he sealed his lips like a tied purse, never counseled aloud, saved his skin, and withdrew—such men!
proposals.reason: Chinese 伊、呂 names Yi Yin and Lü Wang; yiyin day is a fused corruption, not a date.

proposals.before: When Wang Li later fell, Zhai had Chen Xian packed off to his home commandery, where he died of shame.
proposals.after: When Wang Li later fell, Zhai had Chen Xian packed off to his home commandery, where he died of grief.
proposals.reason: Chinese 憂死 is death from grief or anxiety, not shame.

proposals.before: Later General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Yin governed and favored Chen Tang.
proposals.after: At that time General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Yin governed and favored Chen Tang.
proposals.reason: Chinese 時 marks contemporaneity, not later; 車騎將軍 is Wang Yin title.

decisions.reason: The Chinese places the clash 至長樂西闕下, the west towers of Changle Palace; Weiyang is a substitution, and the proposed Changle wording is otherwise unchanged and grammatical.
The literal line likewise renders 長樂 as Weiyang; replacing it with Changle Palace restores the named palace without other invention.
The title is 貳師將軍, not 大將軍; General-in-chief conflates the offices, and Ershi General is the accurate replacement.

當何罷哉 is a rhetorical question about what penalty could fall on the emperor's son for a mistaken killing, not a sentence of official dismissal; the proposed wording matches that sense and the idiomatic line.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 天子之子過誤殺人，當何罷哉

decisions.reason: 廢王更立 means to depose the king and enthrone another; ‘a worthier Liu’ adds both a clan name and a moral ranking absent from the Chinese.
The Chinese says only 立宣帝; Liu Bingyi is an inserted personal name, and ‘established Emperor Xuandi’ restores the source wording.
北掖門 is the north side (掖) palace gate; ‘vee’ is not a reading of 掖, and ‘north side gate’ is accurate without rewriting the rest of the sentence.
廷尉定國 is Dingguo; Dinggu drops 國, and Yu Dingguo is the correct given-name restoration.
The same 定國 appears in the literal line; Dingguo is the required correction and the rest of the sentence is sound.
呼烏烏 is the Qin onomatopoeic cry; ‘day’ is not in the Chinese, and ‘wu-wu’ restores the refrain.
種一頃豆 is one qing of beans, not a hundred; the numeral change is required and otherwise leaves the line intact.

decisions.after: Xian had always been on good terms with Yun; Yun made inquiries, and Xian instructed him to memorialize in self-defence.
decisions.reason: The original reverses roles: 雲從刺候 has Yun inquiring, and the next clause plus 咸漏洩省中語 show Xian prompting Yun to file a self-defence. The proposal correctly makes Yun the petitioner but leaves 教令 agentless (‘was instructed’), so the literal still understates who taught him to appeal.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 咸素善雲，雲從刺候，教令上書自訟

decisions.reason: 伊、呂 are the exemplary ministers Yi Yin and Lü Wang; ‘yiyin day’ is a fused corruption, not a sexagenary date.
以憂死 is death from grief or anxiety; shame is not in the Chinese, and the proposed ‘grief’ matches both the graph and the literal line.
時 marks the same moment, not a later stage; changing Later to At that time corrects the adverb while leaving the rest of the human wording in place.

claimRetractions.reason: The personal name Liu Bingyi is present only in the bad English of s0143; the Chinese 立宣帝 supports the temple-name already extracted as c0302, not a given name in this unit.

claimRevisions.reason: The unit names 定國; the extracted English personal name Dinggu dropped the final syllable and must be Dingguo. The identification remains valid.
